name: Premature Stop Codon Readthrough
therapeuticGoalDescription: Promote ribosomal readthrough of a premature termination codon (PTC) using an ASO that modulates ribosome behavior at the stop site, producing full-length functional protein from a nonsense-mutant transcript.
molecularDefect: Nonsense mutations (premature stop codons) that truncate the protein and cause loss of function.
diseaseMechanism: An ASO targeting sequences near the premature stop codon (in the coding sequence or 3' UTR) modulates ribosome decoding at the PTC, promoting incorporation of a near-cognate tRNA and continuation of translation past the stop codon. This produces full-length protein from the otherwise non-functional transcript.
suitableVariantTypes: Nonsense mutations (premature stop codons); selected splicing mutations that create in-frame PTCs.
typicalDiseases: Cystic fibrosis (nonsense mutations in CFTR); Duchenne muscular dystrophy (nonsense mutations in dystrophin); nonsense mutation disorders generally.
rnaTargetRegion: Coding sequence surrounding the PTC; 3' UTR downstream of the PTC; ribosome decoding center context.
transcriptRequirement: Transcript containing a premature termination codon amenable to readthrough modulation.
asoChemistry: RNase H-inactive ASOs (PMO, 2'-MOE) to modulate ribosome behavior without degrading the transcript.
designRules: Identify PTC location; design ASOs targeting sequences flanking the PTC that influence ribosome decoding; validate readthrough efficiency by Western blot and functional assays.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible coding region near the PTC for ASO binding.
offTargetConsiderations: Potential suppression of normal stop codons (readthrough at native terminators); evaluate specificity for PTC vs. native stop codons.
advantages: Rescues endogenous full-length protein from nonsense transcripts; does not require exogenous protein delivery; leverages existing cellular machinery.
limitations: Readthrough efficiency is typically low (1-10%); may produce readthrough products with altered C-terminal sequences; PTC position and context strongly influence efficiency; no approved therapies.
fdaApprovedDrugs: None (Ataluren/PTC124 was investigated but failed Phase 3 for CF and DMD)
clinicalTrialExamples: Ataluren (PTC124) for CF and DMD (failed Phase 3); ELX-02 for CF (clinical development); synthetic antisense readthrough approaches (preclinical).

evidenceLevel.note: Multiple clinical programs attempted with small-molecule readthrough agents; antisense-based readthrough is preclinical. Ataluren failure raises questions about readthrough as a strategy.
